overview.title: Global Foreign Exchange Committee
overview.definition: The Global Foreign Exchange Committee (GFXC) is a forum of central banks and private sector foreign exchange committees established in 2017 to promote a robust, liquid, open, and appropriately transparent global foreign exchange market.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC Civil Services Prelims (GS-1/Economy regarding international financial architecture, BIS, RBI) and Mains GS Paper III (External Sector, International Financial Institutions, Global Governance, and Financial Stability).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Global Foreign Exchange Committee.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Role of Central Banks and Bank for International Settlements (BIS)

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Establishment & Genesis**: Formed in **May 2017** following a comprehensive review and strengthening of local foreign exchange committees globally under the auspices of the **Bank for International Settlements (BIS)** in Basel, Switzerland.
• **Primary Mandate**: To identify and address structural issues in global FX markets, promote adherence to the **FX Global Code**, and foster communication among local foreign exchange committees (FXCs).
• **Structural Composition**: Comprises representatives from major regional Foreign Exchange Committees globally, including the **Reserve Bank of India's (RBI)** regional committees, alongside key financial sector participants.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The FX market operates on an Over-The-Counter (OTC) basis with daily global turnover exceeding **$7.5 trillion** (according to the BIS Triennial Survey), making global governance and voluntary codes critical for systemic stability.

items.definition: A common set of guidelines providing market participants with standards of good practice covering ethics, governance, execution, information sharing, risk management, and confirmation.
A formal public sign-off by market participants (both buy-side and sell-side) declaring their alignment and adherence to the principles of the FX Global Code.
International financial organization owned by central banks which fosters international monetary and financial cooperation and serves as bank for central banks; houses GFXC.
Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA, 1999) in India, RBI's Internal Working Groups on Forex markets, and international bodies like IOSCO and FSB.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Global Financial Centers**: London (UK), New York (USA), Singapore, Hong Kong, and Tokyo account for the vast majority of global FX turnover.
• **Emerging Hubs**: Mumbai (India) via IFSC Gift City and regional central bank frameworks expanding domestic currency settlement and international trade integration.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Fragmentation of liquidity, algorithmic/high-frequency trading risks, lack of mandatory statutory enforcement globally, and operational risks in settlement.
• **Policy Interventions**: Regular tripartite reviews of the FX Global Code, integration of ESG factors into FX trading, and adoption of robust adherence mechanisms.

items.title: Mnemonic for GFXC Core Pillars
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **E-G-E-I-R** (Every Good Execution Inspires Reliability)
• **Decoded Meaning**: **E**thics, **G**overnance, **E**xecution, **I**nformation sharing, **R**isk management.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly identifies the core code principles when evaluating multi-statement questions.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: GFXC = **Voluntary Code + BIS Secretariat + Central Bank + Private Partnership**. Never confuse it with a legally binding treaty or IMF/World Bank lending arm.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often traps aspirants by stating that the Global Foreign Exchange Committee or the FX Global Code is a legally binding international treaty with penal sanctions. Remember: Adherence to the FX Global Code is entirely **voluntary**, relying on market discipline and public Statements of Commitment.

Mains Value Addition: In answers concerning exchange rate volatility, capital account convertibility, or financial stability (GS-3), cite the role of international standard-setting bodies like the GFXC and BIS in promoting market integrity without distorting capital flows.

keyTakeaways: The Global Foreign Exchange Committee (GFXC) operates under the auspices of the BIS to promote integrity, transparency, and liquidity in global forex markets.
The cornerstone of GFXC's framework is the FX Global Code, which relies on voluntary adherence and public Statements of Commitment rather than statutory regulation.
UPSC aspirants must carefully distinguish between voluntary market codes (GFXC) and legally binding international financial regulations.
